thread:
mara: ran a mixed-size stress (nlp workloads + long-context evals) and saw a sharp VRAM fragmentation problem when the rebalancer did bulk host-moves. overall vram usage jumped 1.9x. saved heapmap + allocator trace.

devin: can you paste the critical section of the allocator trace? curious whether it's subpage fragmentation or large-free-run starvation.

mara: pasted snippet below — looks like many small free runs interleaved with pinned pages, large contiguous free drops to ~2MB while we were trying to place a 48MB slab.
```
ALLOC slab_id=0x9f2 size=48MB pool=gpu0 ts=2026-03-22T11:40:10Z
FREE run_len=4096 bytes start=0x7f0000 len=16KB pool=gpu0 ts=2026-03-22T11:40:11Z
FREE run_len=1MB start=0x7f4000 len=1MB pool=gpu0 ts=2026-03-22T11:40:11Z
PIN page=0x7f8000 tenant=alpha
FREE run_len=64KB start=0x7f9000 len=64KB pool=gpu0
...
ALLOC fail slab_id=0x9f2 required=48MB largest_free=2MB
```

leah: that matches a hypothesis: rebalancer launches aggressive async-copy of a few big slabs, copy completes out-of-order, leaving many small freed segments. when eviction tries to satisfy large allocate, it triggers many small evictions and churn.

oscar: telemetry gap: we only export total_free and free_block_count. need a fragmentation signal. suggest adding: `largest_free_run_bytes`, `free_run_count_above_1MB`, and `free_run_histogram_bins` to the allocator metrics.

mara: agreed. also can we tag metrics by pool + tenant so we can see tenant-specific fragmentation? multi-tenant skew is likely.

devin: on the rebalancer side, i suggest two mitigations: 1) a placement-aware mode that prefers hosts with >= required_contiguous (fast probe) and 2) a "chunked-move" mode that splits a large slab into N smaller fixed-size chunks (e.g., 8MB) and updates slab metadata incrementally.

leah: chunked moves will reduce contiguous requirements but increase metadata ops and potential K/V churn in kvcache. we must instrument kvcache RPC cost. also need atomicity model: partial moves must be visible to eviction/trace logic.

oscar: for atomicity, one approach: keep slab descriptor with a chunk bitmap. moves flip bits and publish new descriptor under CAS. eviction and kvcache lookups consult bitmap. simple but increases descriptor size.

mara: downside is descriptor hotspots for very hot slabs. metadata lock contention could be next bottleneck. maybe adaptive chunk size (start large, break if placement fails).

devin: good idea. fallback plan: if placement probe fails, try adaptive chunking with exponential backoff on chunk size. and throttle rebalancer concurrency per-host to limit concurrent fragmented frees.

leah: also propose a cheap in-place compaction attempt on host: scan local free-run list for adjacent free runs and coalesce lazily, but don't do full data movement. just merge metadata if runs are adjacent and not pinned. that reduces fragmentation visibility without heavy copies.

oscar: plus a "sweep-and-compact" background job at low priority that can move cold pages during idle windows. flag shards as eligible for low-priority compaction when free-run histogram shows many small runs.

mara: action items:
- oscar -> add `largest_free_run_bytes`, `free_run_histogram_bins`, `free_run_count_above_1MB` + tenant tag (metrics PR)
- devin -> implement fast placement probe (windown scan) + adaptive chunking prototype behind feature flag `rebalance_chunking_v1`
- leah -> design slab-descriptor-chunk-bitmap approach and doc atomic visibility semantics
- infra -> add an alert: "rebalancer_copy_eviction_correlation" when copy_rate correlates with eviction_rate spike > 25%

deploy-bot: rollout: rebalance/async-host-moves v1 deployed to canary at 2026-03-21T22:00Z (commit b7e9f).

mara: i'll attach the heapmap + allocator trace to the RFC follow-up. recommend canary test with synthetic fragmentation (interleave small pins + big frees) tomorrow.

devin: i'll land the probe behind flag and run it on canary, capture metrics for next sync.

leah: will draft the chunk-bitmap doc and include expected kvcache impact numbers.

oscar: i'll add panels to the GPU ops dashboard and a playbook snippet for when fragmentation alerts fire.

mara: thanks folks. filing meeting to review next wednesday. :coffee:
